source: Lineup roles from the supplied NPC sheet; personal pressures from QUEST_AND_STORY_DESIGN_v02.md section 8. Ambient lines only: no flags, trust or inventory are granted by these conversations.

HarborClerk.speaker: Enna
HarborClerk.title: Port records and permits
lines: Port records and permits. Everyone sheltering tonight passes through this book.
A name in a ledger can bring a family back together. It can also bring the wrong person to their door.
So who decides what goes in?
The person whose name it is. That is the only rule I trust.

Tavi.speaker: Tavi
Tavi.title: The quay
lines: Tavi. I carry whatever comes off the boats. Tonight it's mostly people's lives in sacks.
My brother will come looking for me. I haven't decided what I want him to find.

Boatwright.speaker: Boatwright
Boatwright.title: The slipway
lines: Three hulls to caulk before the tide turns, and half the street wants my hands for their roofs.
An hour, yes. Not a promise I can't keep. A boat that leaks because I was elsewhere drowns someone too.

Fisherwoman.speaker: Fisherwoman
Fisherwoman.title: The breakwater
lines: Someone saw a light past the breakwater and shouted that it was a warning.
It's a boat coming home with a cracked lamp. I know that rhythm.
Rumors sink more boats than storms. Ask before you repeat what you hear on this quay.

Carpenter.speaker: Carpenter
Carpenter.title: Timber for the night
lines: A patch that holds until morning isn't a repair. I'll tell them which one they're getting.

Baker.speaker: Baker
Baker.title: The bakery counter
lines: Half-loaves for the dock crews, whole ones for the shelter.
If the tally doesn't say which, somebody gets blamed for a loaf that was never missing.
If you're hungry, ask. I'd rather count a gift than chase a rumor.

Archivist.speaker: Archivist
Archivist.title: The archive desk
lines: The display says what it says. A summary repeated a hundred times is still one source.
If you want to know what happened, find what was written on the day.
lines_chronology: You've read the public chronology. Good. Now don't let the plaque do your thinking.
A date in a summary is someone's conclusion. Look for the record it was drawn from.
lines_register: This says they were turning people away before the attack.
It could have been the storm order.
Then you need the original. Not another summary.

ShrineKeeper.speaker: Shrine keeper
ShrineKeeper.title: The memorial lamps
ShrineKeeper.prompt: E  Talk to the shrine keeper
lines: People come to light a lamp for names they're not sure of. I don't tell them they're wrong.
I tell them what we know, and what we don't. A memorial is a promise to remember. It isn't proof of what happened.

LanternKeeper.speaker: Lantern keeper
LanternKeeper.title: The landing lamps
LanternKeeper.prompt: E  Talk to the lantern keeper
lines: Someone has to keep the landings lit, whether the city is grieving or celebrating.
The catch on the landing lamp keeps slipping. One more thing to mend before dark.
